scope: Proposition 2.3 (The pairing supplied by holes) of the manuscript “A Counterexample to Kaplansky's Direct-Finiteness Conjecture in Characteristic Two” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-Direct-Finiteness-Conjecture-in-Characteristic-Two-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 197 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a97d7915d43b5112), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let q ≥ 4 be a power of two, let Q be a field of order q, fix an enumeration of Q, and let n ≥ 1. Put d0 = (q − 2)/2, S = Sd0 ⊂ A = Qn, and Npt = qn. Let ℓ be an odd prime and D = ℓ + 1. Suppose that O ⊂ S and that F is a family of full affine Q-lines contained in V = A \ O, with 2Npt D2 ≤ |O| ≤ 7Npt D2 . (2.1) Suppose also that every point of V lies on D members of F and that the incidence graph has girth at least 12. If K is a finite extension of Q containing a primitive ℓth root of unity, then, with m = |O| and t = |V |, there are columns xv ∈ Km, v ∈ V , such that 0 < m < t ≤ mℓ2 , ∑︂ v∈V xvxT v = −Im, ∑︂ v∈f xvxT v = 0 (f ∈ F).
